% figure registry (figdefs.tex is generated by the extract step)
\newcommand{\qfigdef}[4]{\@namedef{qf@file@#1}{#2}\@namedef{qf@w@#1}{#3}\@namedef{qf@wide@#1}{#4}}
\newcommand{\qf@check}[1]{\@ifundefined{qf@file@#1}{\PackageError{score2}{Unknown figure id #1}{}}{}}
\newcommand{\qf@img}[4][]{\includegraphics[width=#2\dimexpr\@nameuse{qf@w@#4}pt\relax,max width=#3,max height=0.45\textheight,#1]{\@nameuse{qf@file@#4}}}
% Full-width questions: finalize wraps every question that contains a wide figure in \qfullbegin...\qfullend,
% so the WHOLE question (stem, figures, options) is set across the page in reading order, then the two columns
% resume. The question's head - its number, stem and first figure (\qfullsplit marks the end of the head) -
% is kept on one page, so a number is never left at a page foot with its figure overleaf; the rest may break
% across pages normally, so no big gaps are left. Without a \qfullsplit, the whole question is kept together
% if it is under 45% of a page. Never write these yourself.
\newif\ifqf@full
\newif\ifqf@boxed
\newsavebox{\qf@box}
\newcommand{\qf@open}{\global\qf@fulltrue\par\global\qf@boxedtrue
  \setbox\qf@box\vbox\bgroup\hsize\textwidth\linewidth\textwidth}
\newcommand{\qf@emit}[1]{\par\egroup\global\qf@boxedfalse
  \ifdim\dimexpr\ht\qf@box+\dp\qf@box\relax<#1\textheight\noindent\usebox{\qf@box}\par\else\unvbox\qf@box\fi}
\newcommand{\qfullsplit}{\ifqf@boxed\qf@emit{0.85}\fi}
\newcommand{\qf@close}{\ifqf@boxed\qf@emit{0.45}\fi\global\qf@fullfalse}
\newcommand{\qfullbegin}{\end{multicols}\qf@open}
\newcommand{\qfullend}{\qf@close\begin{multicols}{2}}
\newcommand{\qfullstart}{\qf@open}
\newcommand{\qfulldone}{\qf@close}
% \qfig[scale]{id}: block figure, centred, directly where it is written (size set by the tool).
% Fallback if a wide figure is not inside a full-width question: break out of the columns in place - no floats.
\newcommand{\qfig}[2][1]{\qf@check{#2}%
  \ifqf@full\qf@blk{#1}{#2}\else
  \ifnum\@nameuse{qf@wide@#2}=1 \expandafter\@firstoftwo\else\expandafter\@secondoftwo\fi
  {\end{multicols}\begin{center}\qf@img{#1}{\textwidth}{#2}\end{center}\begin{multicols}{2}}%
  {\qf@blk{#1}{#2}}\fi}
\newcommand{\qf@blk}[2]{\par\smallskip{\centering\qf@img{#1}{\linewidth}{#2}\par}\smallskip}
% \qfigi[scale]{id}: inline figure (inside option lists / tables / minipages); never breaks columns.
\newcommand{\qfigi}[2][1]{\qf@check{#2}\qf@img[valign=c]{#1}{\linewidth}{#2}}
\makeatother

\papersec{1}
\partsec{1}{PHYSICS}
\sect{SECTION-I (i)}
\qn{1} Two collars, A of mass 2m and B of mass 3m are connected by a massless rod with pinjoints so that they are constrained to move along the fixed perpendicular rods on horizontal plane as shown, in the accompanying figure. Another collar C of mass m hits A with speed `v' and sticks to it. There is no friction between collars and rods.\par
\qfig{p1_phy_s1_q01_1}
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{The speed of collar C just after the impact is $\dfrac{v\cos^2\alpha}{3}$}
\opt{B}{The speed of collar A just after the impact is $\dfrac{v\sin^2\alpha}{3}$}
\opt{C}{The speed of collar B just after the impact is $\dfrac{v\sin2\alpha}{6}$}
\opt{D}{The speed of collar B just after the impact is $\dfrac{v\cos2\alpha}{3}$}
\end{qoptions}
\qn{2} A non-relativistic particle of mass m is held in a circular orbit around the origin by an attractive force. The potential energy of the force is given by U (r) = $\dfrac{kr^2}{2}$, where r is the distance of the particle from origin and k is a constant. Assuming the Bohr quantization of the angular momentum of the particle, choose the \textbf{correct} (v $\rightarrow$ velocity of particle, KE(r) $\rightarrow$ kinetic energy of particle, E(r) $\rightarrow$ total energy of the particle)
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{r$^2$ = $\dfrac{\text{nh}}{2\pi\sqrt{\text{km}}}$}
\opt{B}{v$^2$ = $\dfrac{\text{nh}}{2\pi\sqrt{\text{km}}}$}
\opt{C}{KE(r) = U(r)}
\opt{D}{E (r) = $\dfrac{\text{nh}}{2\pi}\sqrt{\dfrac{\text{k}}{\text{m}}}$}
\end{qoptions}
\qn{3} A rectangular frame of negligible resistance with capacitor of capacitance C is placed nearby an infinitely long wire carrying current I = I$_0$ sin$\left(\omega\text{t}+\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)$, wire and frame being in same plane. Select correct alternative(s):\par
\qfig{p1_phy_s1_q03_1}
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{Maximum charge on capacitor is $\left(\dfrac{4\mu_0\text{i}_0\omega\,\ln2}{\pi}\right)$ C}
\opt{B}{Charge on capacitor at t = 0 is $\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}\mu_0\text{i}_0\omega\,\ln2}{\pi}\right)$ C}
\opt{C}{Current in frame is minimum at t = $\dfrac{\pi}{3\omega}$}
\opt{D}{Maximum current in frame is $\left(\dfrac{2\omega^2\mu_0\text{i}_0\,\ln2}{\pi}\right)$ C}
\end{qoptions}
\qn{4} In a resistance wire of unit length and unit cross sectional area, resistivity varies as P = $\dfrac{\text{P}_0}{1+\text{x}}$. This wire is connected across a battery of emf V.\par
\qfig{p1_phy_s1_q04_1}
A and B are two ends of the wire and C is mid- point. Choose the \textbf{correct} options ?
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{current I = $\dfrac{\text{V}}{\text{P}_0\ln2}$}
\opt{B}{Electric field at A = $\dfrac{\text{V}}{\ln2}$}
\opt{C}{Electric field at B = $\dfrac{3\text{V}}{2\ln2}$}
\opt{D}{Electric field at C = $\dfrac{2\text{V}}{3\ln2}$}
\end{qoptions}
\qn{5} In Young's double slit experiment at time t = 0, A is central maxima and B is 4$^\text{th}$ maxima. Separation between slits and screen is increasing at a constant speed v. Then for a later time `t'. Choose the \textbf{correct} option.\par
\qfig{p1_phy_s1_q05_1}
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{At t = $\dfrac{\text{x}}{\text{v}}$, B will be 2$^\text{nd}$ order maxima}
\opt{B}{At t = $\dfrac{2\text{x}}{\text{v}}$, B will be 1$^\text{st}$ maxima}
\opt{C}{At t = $\dfrac{5\text{x}}{3\text{v}}$, B will be 2$^\text{nd}$ minima}
\opt{D}{At t = $\dfrac{7\text{x}}{\text{v}}$, B will be 1$^\text{st}$ minima}
\end{qoptions}
\qn{6} A space capsule is in a circular orbit of radius r$_\text{C}$ about the earth. A short burst from a rocket in the backward direction increases the kinetic energy by 20\% and causes the capsule to enter an elliptical orbit with the point of firing as the perigee; i.e., r$_\text{p}$ = r$_\text{C}$.\par
Then choose the \textbf{CORRECT} statement(s) for further motion of capsule:- (Assume mass of capsule to remain nearly constant)
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{Total mechanical energy of capsule decreases.}
\opt{B}{Time period of capsule will decreases.}
\opt{C}{Distance of apogee from centre of earth is r$_\text{A}$ = 1.5r}
\opt{D}{If mechanical energy before the event (short burst) is E$_\text{i}$ \& final mechanical energy after the event is E$_\text{f}$, then E$_\text{f}$ = 0.8E$_\text{i}$.}
\end{qoptions}
\sect{SECTION-I (ii)}

\qn{9} The electric field E is measured at a point P(0,0,d) generated due to various charge distributions and the dependence of E on d is found to be different for different charge distributions. List-I contains different relations between E and d. List-II describes different electric charge distributions, along with their locations. Match the functions in List-I with the related charge distributions in List-II.\par

\qn{1} Figure shows a cyclic process ABCDBEA performed on an ideal gas. If P$_\text{A}$ = 2 atm.,P$_\text{B}$ =4.5 atm. and P$_\text{C}$ = 6 atm.; V$_\text{E}$ - V$_\text{A}$ = 0.05 litre, find the magnitude of work done by the gas (in J) in the complete process in nearest integer.\par

\partsec{2}{CHEMISTRY}
\sect{SECTION-I (i)}
\qn{1} Which of the following is/are \textbf{correct}?
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{Leaching is the method to remove quantitatively Fe$_2$O$_3$ from red bauxite.}
\opt{B}{In the metallurgy of Aluminium, purified Al$_2$O$_3$ is mixed with Na$_3$AlF$_6$ or CaF$_2$ which lowers the melting point of the mixture and also increases conductivity.}
\opt{C}{Chalcocite and cinnabar are sulphide minerals}
\opt{D}{Self reduction is not possible during metallurgy of Mg.}
\end{qoptions}
\qn{2} Which of the following major organic products produced in the given reactions fails to respond positively in Kjeldahl method of Nitrogen estimation?
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{\qfigi{p1_chem_s1_q02_A}}
\opt{B}{\qfigi{p1_chem_s1_q02_B}}
\opt{C}{\qfigi{p1_chem_s1_q02_C}}
\opt{D}{\qfigi{p1_chem_s1_q02_D}}
\end{qoptions}
\qn{3} The \textbf{CORRECT} statement(s) about the Group-I metals is/are
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{Reactivity of Group-I metals towards water decreases down the group}
\opt{B}{Among the Group-I metals, Li spontaneously reacts with N$_2$ to give a coloured crystalline compound.}
\opt{C}{All the Group-I metal halides are high-melting colourless crystalline solids}
\opt{D}{KCl is more soluble in H$_2$O than NaCl}
\end{qoptions}
\qn{4} \textbf{Correct} statement(s) regarding the following reaction sequence is(are) [Consider only major organic product in every step]\par
\qfig{p1_chem_s1_q04_1}
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{A on treatment with CHCl$_3$/KOH gives a foul-smelling compound.}
\opt{B}{A is basic while B is amphoteric.}
\opt{C}{C is more reactive than B towards alkaline hydrolysis.}
\opt{D}{F is less reactive than E towards nucleophilic aromatic substitution.}
\end{qoptions}
\qn{5} 10 mole of liquid `A' and 10 mole of liquid `B' is mixed in a cylindrical vessel containing a piston arrangement. Initially a pressure of 2 atm is maintained on the solution. Now, the piston is raised slowly and isothermally. Assuming A and B to be completely miscible and forming an ideal solution. P$_\text{A}^0$ = 0.6 atm P$_\text{B}^0$ = 0.9 atm, then choose incorrect answers (Given : $\sqrt{2425}$ = 49.25, $\sqrt{3}$ = 1.73, $\sqrt{2}$ = 1.41)
\begin{qoptions}
